newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Brash says expects no market change due to MPS.
newsitem.headline: Brash says expects no market change due to MPS.

text.p: Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash said on Friday he did not expect market conditions to change as a result of today's Monetary Policy Statement.
Brash said he did not expect that there would be any dramatic effect on the exchange rate or interest rates as a result of the monetary policy statement.
"I would not expect any dramatic change in market conditions as a result of our statement this morning," Brash told reporters following the release of the monetary policy statement.
Commenting on the the fall in the RBNZ's Monetary Conditions Index to 792 just minutes after the bank released its statement, Brash said: "I would not want to react too quickly."
Asked what would happen if the the index dropped to 750 he said: "We'll cross that bridge when we come to it," he said.
